nuclearScienceRule: Science curve (user decision 2026-11-01, docs/progression.md "Science curve and menu order (2026-11-01)", superseding 2026-10-29): early and industrial unlocks (up to 2,500) stay near vanilla; the transition stage (steel, chemistry, machinery, coal power) unlocks at 9,000-20,000, the frontier (hydrogen, cryogenics, archive, oil power, hospital, mission control, deep well) at 25,000-75,000, the launch program at 125,000-200,000 and nuclear at 300,000-600,000, with the 1,000,000 reactor the single last unlock. The 12,000 Materials Laboratory (400 science per working hour) keeps its unlock, so it becomes the transition stage's stepping stone. Order within the stages is unchanged: Uranium Processing Plant, Waste Vault and the radioactive waste export 300,000, Reactor Charging Bay 300,000 (400,000 until 2026-11-03: Reactor Bots exist from the plant's power cells, so their charging bay unlocks with it; docs/deadlock-audit.md D6), Waste Refinery 600,000, reactor 1,000,000. Approved follow-ups (2026-11-01): the radioactive water recovery pump and outfall unlock at 50,000 (frontier) so radioactive tides can be cleaned up before the nuclear stage, and the Grocery Store at 3,000 (industrial).

hospital.patientStay: Admitted until cured: every treatment effect has SatisfyToMaxValue, so native AttractionNeedBehavior returns to the stay until all four conditions are at their maximum. The ward stays open while a crew is assigned (on call day and night) and treats at crew strength; it closes, releasing patients, only without power, crew or patient meals.

patientMeals.policy: Admitted patients cannot leave to eat, so the Hospital stocks every faction food (carried Box goods with a Hunger effect, chosen at runtime) and water, delivered by native haulers, and feeds patients the stocked good native InventoryNeedBehavior would choose. Water covers waterDays for every bed at the zombie rate (zombieNeedMultiplier x native Thirst).

hospital.supplyPolicy: Fixed supplies per staffed, powered operating hour cover the ward and preventive neighborhood care; native fractional supply buffers persist through saves. Staff use none of the thirty patient places.
hospital.rateInterpretation: 80 percent faster recovery means 1.8 times the native Medical Bed healing rate, or 5/9 of its treatment time. It does not mean 80 percent shorter treatment time.

modularWarehouse.status: Generated by create_frontier_expansion_content.mjs (makeModularWarehouse, makeWarehouseModule) from the late-game studies of both buildings (tools/lategame_batches.json); behaviour in src/DeepFrontier/Scripts/ModularStorage; not built or tested in game
modularWarehouse.design: One core that haulers use and Warehouse Modules attached to it. A finished module is attached when it touches the finished core or an attached module face to face: side by side, or stacked on its top. The core is the network's one storage point (one native inventory); modules hold no goods and have no entrance. Open slots = 1 + attached modules, at most maxSlots; capacity = the core's plus each module's, shared equally by the open slots. Each slot is a warehouse of its own: one good and the native Accept / Obtain / Supply / Empty setting. Removing a module lowers the capacity; stock above the new shares and the goods of closed slots are native unwanted stock that workers carry to other storage.
modularWarehouse.capacityBasis: vanilla Large Warehouse 1,200 in 3x3x2 at 250 science (67 per cell): a 3x3x1 module holds 600 (67 per cell); the 3x3x2 core holds 600 besides its hall. A core with four modules opens all five slots (3,000, 600 each); every further module adds 600 shared by the five.
